title: Canary accuracy verifier for FP8/INT8 quantization with adaptive prompt sampling
creator: Maya Lin
description: Goal: build a lightweight, CI-integrated canary verifier that validates FP8/INT8 quantized model variants against a compact, high-signal prompt set before automated rollouts. Motivation: full golden-suite runs are expensive and slow; we need a fast gate that catches regressions with high precision and low latency to protect production rollouts and avoid costly rollbacks. Scope: a self-contained harness that runs as a pre-rollout canary job and as a periodic job on dedicated capacity. It should: 1) sample an adaptive subset of golden prompts (per-domain stratification), 2) apply small adversarial perturbations and prompt templates to increase sensitivity to subtle regressions, 3) compute per-prompt and aggregate metrics (exact-match, BLEU-style similarity, embedding cosine delta, top-k token divergences), 4) compare to dynamic thresholds (thresholds that vary by prompt class and model size), 5) output a pass/fail gate, per-prompt diagnostics, and telemetry suitable for Console dashboards and rollout decisions. Out of scope: full-scale regression runs, human-in-the-loop labeling (this harness must be automated). Architecture: lightweight runner (go/python) that orchestrates request generation, batching to quantized endpoint, local diff analysis using reference outputs (golden canonical answers from the verified float model), and a small scoring layer. Results are pushed to a canary results S3 path and a CI artifact; failures create a rollback flag that integrates with the rollout engine. Trade-offs documented: - Sensitivity vs false positives: to reduce false positives we use adaptive sampling amplification (run more variations for low-confidence prompts) and per-prompt thresholds tuned to historical variance. - Cost vs coverage: choose a compact prompt set (~120 prompts) stratified across domains and length buckets. - Latency: run in parallel with aggressive batching but cap request budget to keep CI time < 12 minutes. Success criteria: - Detects known regression signatures from prior quant calibration runs (example datasets in attachments) - False positive rate < 3% on held-out no-regression weeks - CI pass/fail latency < 12 minutes for typical runs - Integrates with rollout system and can trigger automatic pause on failure Delivery plan: - Week 1: prototype runner and adaptive sampling logic - Week 2: metrics layer, integration with CI, dashboard stubs - Week 3: threshold calibration using historical traces, integrate with rollout engine - Week 4: QA and rollout to canary channel Acceptance: see acceptance_criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Canary job runs end-to-end in CI on commit and completes within 12 minutes; 2) On injected regressions (see test payloads), the harness flags failure with clear per-prompt diagnostics; 3) Pass/fail decision serialized to rollout engine API; 4) Telemetry emitted to Console: per-prompt delta histogram, aggregate pass rate, and top-10 divergent prompts; 5) Threshold tuning run and calibration artifacts checked in to confluence and S3

notes: Tuning note: dynamic thresholds computed as baseline_mean + k * baseline_std where k varies by prompt class; initial k values recorded in confluence doc.
Operational note: canary failures should create an incident candidate for on-call only if aggregate failure rate > 5% and top-3 prompts show > 10% divergence in top-1 token probability.
Follow-ups: integrate with model-sensitivity atlas to automatically suggest narrower thresholds for prompts sensitive to specific layers.
